strings.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
strings.role: President of Mexico · Energy science and urban governance
strings.summary: Sheinbaum moved from physics and energy research into public service, serving as Mexico City environment secretary, Tlalpan district head and mayor. She contributed to IPCC assessments and became Mexico’s first woman president in 2024. Her career connects science, urban governance and women’s political representation; her security, trade and institutional policies require assessment alongside their controversies.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 13 November 2026; selected milestones cover 1962–2026. Official November 2026 activity records confirm her public role and living status; this is not an exhaustive policy or controversy record.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: National Autonomous University of Mexico: physics degree and doctorate in energy engineering
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Science and climate assessment
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Contributed to IPCC assessments. The 2007 Peace Prize went to the IPCC as an organisation, not to her individually.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Political representation
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Became the first woman elected mayor of Mexico City and the first woman president of Mexico.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Presents second government report
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Presented her administration’s record; the interior secretary delivered the report to Congress on the government’s behalf.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Takes office as president
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Sworn in for a six-year term after winning the June election, becoming Mexico’s first woman president.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Wins presidential nomination
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Selected to represent MORENA and its coalition in the 2024 presidential election.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Leads Mexico City
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Became the city’s first elected woman mayor, serving until June 2023.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Heads Tlalpan district
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Led the Mexico City district of Tlalpan until 2017.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Contributes to IPCC assessment
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Contributed to the IPCC’s Fourth Assessment Report; the associated Nobel Peace Prize belonged to the organisation.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Becomes environment secretary
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Oversaw environmental affairs in Mexico City’s government until 2006.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Joins university research institute
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Joined UNAM’s Engineering Institute, working on energy and environmental research.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Mexico City
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Later studied physics and energy engineering at UNAM.
